title: Reservation UI and end-to-end flow
idea: The reservation frontend is three screens (search, pick a time, confirmation) driven by one reducer, with an API client that sends an Idempotency-Key so retries never book twice.
points: ReservationPage owns the reducer; children render and dispatch, and ReservationPanel calls apiClient.
Confirm is ignored while SUBMITTING, and a retry reuses the same Idempotency-Key.
A 409 NO_TABLE removes that time; picking another time makes a new key.
Follow-ups: shard by restaurant, add a waitlist, or let hosts join two tables.

code.title: Reservation reducer
code.caption: Pure screen logic. Run it, then add a PICK after BOOKED and predict the output.

walk.text: The whole screen state: step, party size, free times, chosen time, key and error.
A search resets the screen; no free times means an EMPTY step, not a blank list.
Picking a time is a new request, so any old key is dropped.
Confirm works only while CHOOSING, and keeps an existing key.
A failure keeps the key for the retry; a 409 removes the taken time.
The loop makes keys the way the component does: reuse first, else new.

code.title: ReservationPanel component
code.caption: A React component that renders state and dispatches events. Real slots carry ISO times. Not run here.

walk.text: Refuse a second submit, reuse or create the key, then mark SUBMITTING.
Call the API once; 409 NO_TABLE means the time was taken, other failures allow a retry.
Loading and empty results get their own screens, never a blank list.
Errors render in an alert region so screen readers announce them.
The button is disabled with no time picked or while a request is in flight.

pitfalls: Do not make a new Idempotency-Key on retry; that can book two tables for one party.
After a 409, remove the taken time from the list and say why.
At scale, shard reservations by restaurant; overlaps never cross restaurants, so no global lock.

quiz.q: In the run, what key does the third CONFIRM_CLICKED use?
quiz.why: REQUEST_FAILED keeps `key` in state. The next click finds a key already set and reuses rk-1, so a replay cannot double book.

takeaway: One reducer owns the screen; one key per choice makes retries safe.
